newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Arafat in Brussels to sign treaty with EU.
newsitem.headline: Arafat in Brussels to sign treaty with EU.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat arrived in Brussels on Monday for talks with European Union foreign ministers and to sign a lucrative association agreement with the EU.
Diplomats said the agreement -- which offers reduced tariffs for Palestinian exports to the EU -- strengthened the 15-nation bloc's position as the entity's main foreign bankroller.
This position has already led a major human rights group to call for the EU to press Arafat to stop alleged abuses by Palestinian security forces.

Human Rights Watch said on Saturday that under the EU's agreement, the Palestinian Authority should be required to "cease the pattern of legal measures and security force conduct that chills political debate and dissent".

Human Rights Watch executive director Kenneth Roth asked Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo and European Commissioner Manuel Marin to push Arafat to free more than 500 people being detained without charge, or charge and bring them to trial soon.
The Europeans had a special responsibility to lean on Arafat, Roth said, because the EU was the chief source of funds for Palestinian police programmes.
